correctness.rationale: The relative sign chain has rates 2γ from either extreme to 0 and γ from 0 to each extreme. Its common-noise gap flows contract at rate at least μ, preserve the interval of the two extreme equilibria, and can reach neighborhoods throughout it by long extreme dwells and switches. Conditioning on an elapsed holding time gives density away from a mode's own equilibrium; other modes cannot supply an atom at that distinct equilibrium. Extending the integrable stationary mode currents by zero, the distributional transport equations give integrable derivatives and hence zero endpoint currents. If H is the tail mass of the mode attracted to the endpoint, the integrated equations and nonnegativity give H0=O(εH), Hopp=O(ε²H). With inward linearization k, they then give H'/H=(2γ/k)/ε+O(1), proving a positive finite tail constant, the stated density power and its relative remainder. The other pointwise currents give p0/pattr=(k/(2v))ε+O(ε²) and popp/pattr=O(ε²). Substituting k±=2μR/(R±v) proves the regime ordering and equality cases. The supplied example independently gives support [2,4], powers (2/3,4/3) and thresholds (3/4,3/2) in upper-then-lower threshold order. The frozen finite-volume script was read but not run; its fitted exponents are diagnostic only.
